origins.section: 18.3. The TVR Says What the Terminal Saw, and Tag 9F10 What the Card Saw
18.4. A Valid Cryptogram Proves the Card, Not That the Request Is New
18.6. A Card That Declines After an Approval Leaves an Approval to Reverse
18.6. A Card That Declines After an Approval Leaves an Approval to Reverse

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-tvr-bit: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tvr-bit: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tvr-bit: 18.3 says writing bit 7 as 1 << 7 tests 0x80, which is bit 8 ('offline data authentication was not performed'), so the rule fires on a different condition and lets every real failure through, which is option b.
recorded.prompt:q-copied-request: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-request: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-request: 18.4 says the copy verifies, that only the issuer's record of the last ATC verified for the card catches it, and that a counter that repeats from another merchant is a replay, so declining is right.
recorded.prompt:q-aac-after-approval: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-aac-after-approval: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-aac-after-approval: 18.6 says the issuer has approved and holds the amount, and only the acquirer knows the purchase failed, so the acquirer must undo the approval with a reversal.
recorded.prompt:q-contactless-script: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-contactless-script: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-contactless-script: 18.6 (Contactless note) says the card leaves the field before the answer arrives, so a script in template 71 or 72 usually can't reach the card in this purchase.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-tvr-bit:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tvr-bit:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tvr-bit:a: 18.3 (and the 18.8 TVR table) says EMV numbers bits from 8 at the leftmost down to 1, so bit 7 is 0x40 and 1 << 7 tests bit 8; that contradicts the claim that Java and EMV number bits the same way.
recorded.prompt:q-tvr-bit:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tvr-bit:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tvr-bit:c: 18.3 says the 1 << 7 rule lets every real failure through, so the rule does not decline the intended cards; the page never suggests jPOS reorders bits, and 18.2 shows unpacked TLV values read back as sent.
recorded.prompt:q-tvr-bit:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tvr-bit:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tvr-bit:d: 18.3 says the mask tests 0x80, bit 8, and the rule 'fires on a different condition', so the test is sometimes true and the 'overflows, never true' reason is refuted.
recorded.prompt:q-copied-request:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-request:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-request:a: 18.4 ('The copy verifies') says a captured authorization verifies again and could be replayed from another merchant, so a verified cryptogram does not prove the card was present just now.
recorded.prompt:q-copied-request:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-request:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-request:c: 18.4 says a copy carries the counter and unpredictable number unchanged, so the counter is the old one and does not show a new request.
recorded.prompt:q-copied-request:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-request:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-request:d: 18.4's run shows the same bytes sent again verify and return the same ARPC, so the HSM does not accept a cryptogram only once.
recorded.prompt:q-aac-after-approval:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-aac-after-approval:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-aac-after-approval:b: 18.6 says sending the authorization again doesn't help, because the card's decline is final and a new request would be a second purchase while the first approval still holds the money.
recorded.prompt:q-aac-after-approval:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-aac-after-approval:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-aac-after-approval:c: 18.6 says only the acquirer knows the purchase failed and the issuer keeps holding the amount until a reversal arrives or the hold expires, so the issuer did not see the AAC and release the money.
recorded.prompt:q-aac-after-approval:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-aac-after-approval:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-aac-after-approval:d: 18.1 and 18.10 say the card can still decline after an issuer approval, and 18.6 calls this a purchase the merchant could not complete, so the approval is not final and the sale cannot go ahead.
recorded.prompt:q-contactless-script:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-contactless-script:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-contactless-script:a: 18.6 (Contactless note) says most contactless kernels have no second GENERATE AC and template 71 can't reach the card in this purchase either.
recorded.prompt:q-contactless-script:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-contactless-script:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-contactless-script:b: 18.6 (Contactless note) says a script usually can't reach the card in this purchase at all because the card has left the field, which rules out running it at the end of this purchase.
recorded.prompt:q-contactless-script:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-contactless-script:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-contactless-script:d: 18.5 shows the issuer putting scripts into the DE 55 of its 0110/0210 authorization response, not after clearing, so the stated reason is refuted even though the 'not in this purchase' part is right.
